assertions.description: navigator.bluetooth exists — the entry point the whole interface family hangs off. Absent on desktop Linux without the experimental flag, on iOS Chrome, Android WebView, Firefox and Safari.
BluetoothRemoteGATTServer is exposed as a Window global, which is the interface this feature changes.

The direct parent of BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.prototype is exactly EventTarget.prototype — the one line of IDL this feature ships. False on pre-157 builds, where the prototype chains straight to Object.prototype.
addEventListener, removeEventListener and dispatchEvent — the three methods the summary names — all resolve as functions through the server's prototype.

The three methods are inherited, not own properties of BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.prototype, and are the same function objects EventTarget.prototype holds — real Web IDL inheritance, not a polyfill bolting copies on.
assertions.test: typeof BluetoothRemoteGATTServer === 'undefined' ? false : ['addEventListener','removeEventListener','dispatchEvent'].every(function(m){return !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.prototype, m) && BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.prototype[m] === EventTarget.prototype[m];})

assertions.description: The inheritance is additive: the six pre-existing members (device, connected, connect, disconnect, getPrimaryService, getPrimaryServices) remain own members of the prototype.
Migration contract: gattserverdisconnected stays on BluetoothDevice — its ongattserverdisconnected handler attribute remains an own member of BluetoothDevice.prototype after this change.
dispatchEvent() and listener invocation on a live BluetoothRemoteGATTServer instance require a paired device and an active GATT connection, which needs a user gesture and hardware.
assertions.test: Requires a user-gesture requestDevice() flow and a BLE device in range; a server instance cannot be constructed synthetically. Verified interactively via the server-event-listeners concept page.
